title: Introduce econ-autotune feedback workflow and lightweight defaults reconciler
author: Lina Patel
description: Context: customers with mixed bursty and steady workloads need better automated tuning of batching/caching defaults and quantization fallbacks without manual intervention. This PR introduces a feedback-driven autotune workflow that reads runtime econ signals (latency p95, token cost, cache hit ratio, failover count) and proposes adjusted tenant defaults; it also ships a lightweight reconciler that applies safe changes (non-breaking, rate-limited) to batch/cache/quant profiles. Summary of what changed: added econ-feedback service that consumes telemetry from Console/Runtime, a reconciliation controller in the admin plane, small runtime scoring hook to tag requests with candidate signals, and a CLI dry-run mode for operators to simulate applying profile deltas. Checklist: [x] backend service and API contract defined, [x] reconciler implemented with safety caps and cooldowns, [x] runtime scoring hook (non-blocking) added, [x] unit economics heuristics and gating rules included, [x] CLI dry-run and apply paths implemented, [x] e2e smoke test harness, [x] docs PR stub and changelog entry. Motivation: prior autotune attempts applied aggressive profile changes that sometimes regressed tail latency; this design favors conservative, telemetry-driven proposals with explicit operator or automated gating based on evaluation windows and synthetic checks. Risk and mitigations: potential for oscillation mitigated by exponential backoff and minimum-stability window; quantization rollouts are only applied to canary lanes first and will auto-revert if quality degradation is detected. How to validate: run `devctl econ simulate --tenant <id> --window 1h --dry-run` to preview suggestions; see Console -> Tenant Defaults for suggested diffs. Deployment notes: feature flagged behind `econ_autotune_v1`; reconciler disabled by default for on-prem installs. Related: builds on earlier telemetry/metrics work (ENG-3981) and ties into incident playbook SUP-1081 for rollback.

release_notes: Adds a telemetry-driven autotune workflow that generates conservative suggestions for batching, caching, and quantization defaults. Includes a safe reconciler, CLI dry-run, and canary-first rollout mechanics. Feature-flagged. Admin docs included.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps runtime changes to a thin scoring hook to avoid introducing latency. Major logic lives in the control plane service so it can be iterated without runtime deploys. Follow-up planned: metrics-backed rollback automation (ENG-4502).
